I've been working this land for forty years. I know what it wants.

My 10.1 mu splits the way it always has — about 7 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, the other 3 mu for cotton. The wheat-maize land double-crops on itself, so I get three harvests across the year on essentially the same ground.

**Wheat:** I plant in mid-October after the summer maize comes off. I'll use the improved Jimai variety the seed station sells — I've used it for years, it does well here. I plough before planting, same as always. Three irrigations: the winter water before freeze-up, the jointing water in April, and the grain-fill water in May. I'll put down base fertilizer with the planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. Three spray passes — herbicide in winter, then fungicide and aphid spray in spring. Should get around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize:** Goes in right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. Hybrid seed, same brand as last few years. I do rotary tillage after wheat stubble — no time or energy to plough in summer. Three irrigations. Heavy nitrogen because maize drinks it. Two pesticide passes for stem borer and armyworm. Target 550 jin per mu.

**Cotton:** This is the hard one. My son keeps saying drop it, too much work. But I know cotton and those 3 mu still bring decent cash. Hybrid seed, plough in spring. Cotton needs more water and more spraying than anything — I'll irrigate five times and spray seven times for bollworm, aphids, red spider mite. It wears me out but I've been doing it since I was young.
